title: feat: filter model discovery by recent reliability
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Filter public discovery of community proxy models at >80% success across the latest 50 eligible final requests within seven days. Final 4xx are excluded; owner requests, monitor probes, and successful fallback rescues count. Unknown health stays visible.
- Keep official-model and agent health on its existing 24-hour window. Show all automatically filtered models with `reliability=all`; exact-ID calls, fallbacks, permissions, private access, and manual hiding stay unchanged. The public monitor uses this unfiltered view.
- Remove the Play-page uptime dot and its now-unused hook. Update the model dashboard, API descriptions, and provider docs to match the new rule.
- Replace monitor hide/relist writes and the daily audit with selective text/image probes: four-hour base interval, backoff up to six days after server/protocol failures, and the existing 30-minute reply cycle. Daily leaderboard posts include only newly filtered/back-in-listings changes; the first check seeds a baseline.
- Not deployed. Rollout order: validate Tinybird in staging, deploy the pipe to production, deploy Workers, clear only old monitor-owned hides, then install the merged EC2 updater. No D1 schema change; manual hide fields remain.

gist.headline: The garden checks its sprouts
gist.blurb: Community models now earn a place in the public catalog by staying healthy where it counts. Polli stopped trusting a single lucky buzz and started checking the last 50.
gist.summary: Public discovery now lists community proxy models that exceed 80% success across their latest 50 eligible final requests in the past seven days, while unknown-health models remain visible and the full catalog is available with reliability=all.
gist.impact: People browsing models get a catalog biased toward recently dependable community options, while exact-ID calls, fallbacks, private access, permissions, manual hides, and official-model health behavior remain unchanged.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the public model catalog as a cozy garden: healthy code-plants with clear little success gauges are placed on the sunny display shelf, while other plants remain safely visible in a nearby "ALL" greenhouse rather than being discarded. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener hat and holding a clipboard, reviews a row of 50 small request-seed markers beside the eager CRT Monitor Robot, which is gently probing plants on a timed schedule.
